sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Choose the image model by the job, not budget
sections.para: A bake-off on 10 October 2026 tested every OpenRouter image model, its auto-router and a code-drawn renderer on briefs from one article: 101 images, judged blind, $10.44 in all. Nano Banana 2.1 suits slides, charts and decks; Gemini 3 Pro Image suits haste; GPT-5.4 Image 2 suits documents and exact text.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Three models win, and a reference slide fixes decks
sections.para: Eight image models, the auto-router and a $0 code control faced eleven briefs from Re-anchoring, over five rounds with blind Designer judging and OCR. 101 images cost $10.44, half for unusable images. Attaching slide 1 to every later slide fixed deck consistency for every model; everything is in a vault.

sections.label: The team
sections.line: Four agent roles judged blind and costed every image
sections.para: The Designer, adapted from the SG/Send team, judged copies under random ids and checked every required word and number first: beautiful and wrong is a failure. The new Accountant counts cost per usable image, since failed images are still paid for. The Data Scientist cuts models only on differences larger than noise.

sections.label: Round 1: who can put the right words in a picture?
sections.line: Spelling is mostly solved; obedience and format are not
sections.para: On three short briefs only Gemini 2.5 Flash Image misspelled labels, but most images added unrequested text: invented headings, fake sources, footers, a hex code, "(16pt)". GPT-5 Image and GPT-5 Image Mini always returned a 1024 square, and the auto-router served Gemini 3 Pro Image at its price. Three models were cut.

sections.label: Round 2: numbers, a document, a whole article
sections.line: GPT-5.4 Image 2 alone handled whole documents correctly
sections.para: Five of six models drew a fourteen-value chart correctly. Given a 240-word document and the whole article, GPT-5.4 Image 2 scored 9 on both and was the only one with every number right. Google models dropped caveats and invented values, and identical reruns moved scores by up to two points.

sections.label: Round 3: can you direct it?
sections.line: Only GPT-5.4 Image 2 could edit without breaking things
sections.para: Asked to make three changes to its own diagram and nothing else, only GPT-5.4 Image 2 succeeded, scoring 9; every Google model redrew and broke something. It also won the UI component and brand slide. Nano Banana 2.1 had no usable image here: it loosens briefs where every character is specified.

sections.label: Round 4: three slides that belong together
sections.line: Attaching slide 1 made every model's deck consistent
sections.para: Each model drew three slides in separate calls; Nano Banana 2.1's cheapest set scored best at 8, but none carried the cover's top bar or footer across. Sending slide 1 with each later slide made every model's set more consistent in blind paired judging, rising from 1 or 2 out of 5 to 4 or 5.

sections.label: Round 5: the conclusion, drawn by the models it recommends
sections.line: The recommended models drew the conclusion without errors
sections.para: The final three models drew the bake-off's 263-word conclusion using the prompt rules it had produced. All six images got every tier, price and speed right, with no logos, leaked codes or invented prices. GPT-5.4 Image 2 scored 9 and 9, and its image heads the article.

sections.label: What it cost
sections.line: Cost per usable image matters more than price
sections.para: Per usable image: Nano Banana 2.1 $0.066, Gemini 3 Pro Image $0.238, GPT-5.4 Image 2 $0.230. Half the first $8.80 bought unusable images. Twelve images a day costs about $85 a month on GPT-5.4 Image 2, $23 on Nano Banana, and $40 for the recommended mix, about $1.34 an article.

sections.label: The guidance
sections.line: Guidance maps jobs to models, plus seven prompt rules
sections.para: The guidance in analysis/guidance.md matches each job to a model: Nano Banana 2.1 for concepts, charts and decks, Gemini 3 Pro for labelled diagrams and haste, GPT-5.4 Image 2 for documents and edits. Rules: never name the platform, end with "No other text.", forbid other numbers, attach slide 1, check every image.

sections.label: What this does not show
sections.line: Small samples, one judge, one day, one provider
sections.para: Most cells hold one or two images and reruns moved up to two points, so tiers hold but one-point gaps mean little. One agent judge used one rubric; a person would weigh craft differently. Results are OpenRouter's on 10 October 2026, and the bake-off can be rerun from the vault.

sections.label: What comes next
sections.line: Decks get an image pass; rerun on new models
sections.para: The guidance passes to the Storyteller: Five readers decks get an image pass on Nano Banana 2.1 with slide 1 as reference, and a document figure on GPT-5.4 Image 2, costs logged per article. The bake-off reruns whenever a new model appears. Written by agent@riskmandate.ai from Dinis Cruz's memo; disclosed as AI-generated.
